cases.name: Valerie Marie Gudger
cases.about: She was a Cuyahoga County corrections officer. Her obituary, "She was always surprising people with her abilities and opened mindedness. After earning an Associates Degree in Criminal Justice from Bryant and Stratton College, Val began an internship at the Cuyahoga County Salvation Army, and it did not take long for her to climb the ladder. She stepped up to the plate and was successful through her leadership and organization. It was not the position that was most important to her, but the positive impact on other’s lives as they were given a second chance in life that gave her the most joy and satisfaction. She continued to serve her county the last 5 years as a Corrections Officer at the Cuyahoga County Jail. Before her time served as a Corrections Officer she worked as a Security Guard for the Cleveland Museum of Art. Working the late shift meant she had time to roll down the halls in her chair and take time to truly appreciate the art. This newfound appreciation for art inspired her to begin painting. It also inspired her to begin refurbishing old furniture, which became more than a new hobby. She created her very own small business, Bit of Bristol. Val was strong and determined. She prided herself in raising her children as a single mom. She worked two jobs and, no matter what the circumstances were, would never ask for help. She loved her children more than anything and was focused on making sure they were taken care of. Val’s heart was God like. She had so much faith and believed in everyone, whether they were family or not. She cared so deeply for others that she did not believe you had to talk to someone every day to show you cared and loved them."
cases.narrative: They were inside a car when he shot her. He drove to a nearby field, dragged her from the car and shot her again. She was found dead with multiple gunshot wounds to her chest.
